key_insight: Model choice drives AI peer-review accuracy most strongly, while verification tools offer targeted gains that depend on the research domain.
engineering_relevance: Peer-review systems should benchmark their base models and add citation retrieval, computer algebra, and code execution where these improve error detection.
method: Inject localisable errors across four categories and three severity levels into real papers.
Measure detection by category and severity, plus false positives on clean copies.
Compare 12 reviewer systems, including Skepthical’s multi-agent, tool-assisted verification.
evidence_signal: Across 30 astrophysics and ML preprints with 357 injected errors, three frontier models using the same prompt differed by about 50 percentage points in overall detection on both corpora.
watch_item: Results come from two small corpora with injected errors; Skepthical’s strong citation-detection advantage in astrophysics did not carry over to ML.
paper_title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
